prompt:
I need the front end for Codecairn. A spatial map of a software codebase, kept by the volunteer tech team of a small food-rescue nonprofit so newcomers can see how their app's parts are arranged and connected before they change anything.

Who's using it: Wen Liu, a backend developer at an insurance company who volunteers four hours a week with Second Helping, a nonprofit that sends volunteer drivers to collect surplus food from restaurants and take it to shelters. It's her second week on the team.

What they're doing right now: The coordinator reported that drivers in the east zone are getting pickup windows an hour off after the clocks changed. Wen has been asked to find where pickup scheduling and time zones are handled. She is exploring the map of the codebase. Modules sit close together when they call each other a lot, and services are grouped into regions. She is trying to trace the path from the driver's text-message reminder back to where the pickup window is calculated, and to work out which nearby modules she'd be risking if she changed it. She also wants to see who last worked in that area so she can ask them.

What's in the system at this point: Repository 'second-helping' with 3 services: the dispatch API (Python, 142 modules), the driver SMS worker (Node, 38 modules) and the donor web app (34 modules), 214 modules in total. Each module records its path, size in lines (20–2,900), test coverage (0–94%), last modified date, last volunteer to touch it, and the modules it calls or imports (612 dependency links). Relevant modules include dispatch/scheduling/windows.py (1,140 lines, 31% coverage, last touched by Marco D. in March 2025), dispatch/util/tz.py (88 lines, 0% coverage), sms/reminders/compose.js (last touched by Wen's onboarding buddy Ruth A. in September 2026), and dispatch/zones/east.py. Open issues pinned to locations: 9, including #212 'DST pickup offset east zone' opened Nov 3, 2026. Active volunteers on the tech team: 6. Hosting is a single donated VPS.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
